analysis.title: AI Default Risk Triples Since Jan As Goldman Clients See "A Crisis Without A Crisis"
key_insights: Goldman FICC's Reid Zhou (note "From Macro to Micro", published late Thursday Oct 29, 2026) reports London client meetings with a directionless, bearish-tilted credit mood. Gross positioning is light, and a squeeze tighter would be painful for most.

Long equity/short credit and decomp are the consensus medium-term trades, with cash credit viewed as an asymmetric short at current valuations. Most clients concede a rally into year end is the most likely outcome, but few are positioned for it.

Goldman data on the past decade of CDX IG shows the median 1-month forward spread change is closest to zero when IG trades between 60bps and 65bps, so credit has historically been a coin flip at these levels.

This is the third AI-driven credit scare of 2026: February (private credit exposure to AI disruption), July (hyperscaler bond supply), and now (whether companies can afford higher funding costs). The market is moving from macro to micro, with each earnings print and new issue separating issuers.

CDX IG and HY have retraced from 2026 wides (69th and 74th percentile) to the high 50s percentile, and HYG is at the 10th percentile. USD CCC cash spreads are at the 96th percentile, versus the 51st percentile at the 2026 wides.
CCC spreads are at 1,157bps, up 338bps YTD and 195bps in three months, while the HY index is only 20bps wider YTD.

In IG, Technology is 50bps wider YTD (to 144bps), Telecoms +44bps and Media +44bps, while Health Care (+1bp), Industrials (+4bps) and Oil & Gas (-10bps) barely moved. In HY, Telco is 219bps wider to 599bps YTD, Tech is 34bps wider in the past month, and Oil & Gas is 108bps tighter.

Zhou expects the next wave of AI concern to focus on the demand/ROI side (whether capex returns will be large and fast enough), and does not think one should turn bearish on AI solely because of the recent scares.

Amazon reported Q3 capex of $77.3B (up 43% from Q2), free cash flow of -$33.5B, and raised $48.1B of new long-term debt in the quarter. Its long-term debt has nearly tripled in nine months to $173.1B. The stock fell as much as 12.5% after hours despite AWS growing at its fastest pace in nearly five years.
Microsoft launched a $25B bond deal the morning after its earnings beat, and Alphabet had its worst day ever as hyperscaler credit went "back in scary mode" (per the article).

Goldman attributes the latest AI selloff to oil and rates: higher inflation prints from persistently high oil prices imply a more restrictive policy path, which sold off rates and raised corporate funding concerns. Headline inflation is 4.02% while core is about 2.8%.
The market prices roughly 80% odds of another Fed hike in December after the September hike and Wednesday's pause. The market shaved about 10bps off 2027 terminal-rate pricing on Thursday.

Goldman sees markets treating $100 oil as transitory, trading as if a US-Iran deal will come soon. A deal could drop oil immediately and trigger a risk rally, while escalation would hurt the economy through energy prices.
Zhou sees the Fed pause as a clearing event and expects some near-term relief on funding costs. Goldman remains cautiously optimistic going into year end.

Goldman's 3Y AI CDS basket is about 100bps, nearly triple the ~35bps at the start of the year, while the NDX 1-year 10-delta put is about 505 versus a June peak near 590. Credit protection has become much more expensive than equity protection for hyperscalers.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 capex of $77.3B and free cash flow of -$33.5B against an expected outflow of about $7.7B (per the article's garbled text), funded by $48.1B of new debt. The stock fell as much as 12.5% after hours.
Launched a $25B bond deal the morning after a clean earnings beat.
Described as having its worst day ever as hyperscaler credit moved back into scary mode.

sector_views.rationale: Tech IG spreads are 50bps wider YTD to 144bps and HY Tech is 34bps wider in the past month on AI debt and ROI concerns.
HY Telco spreads are 219bps wider YTD to 599bps.

earnings_insights: Amazon Q3 (reported Oct 29-30, 2026): capex $77.3B (+43% vs Q2), free cash flow -$33.5B reported, versus a garbled expected outflow figure in the text (appears to be about $7.7B expected, with trailing FCF of about -$42.4B referenced). AWS growth was its fastest in nearly five years. $48.1B of new long-term debt raised in the quarter, bringing long-term debt to $173.1B.
Microsoft: described as a 'clean' beat, followed by a $25B bond deal the next morning. No EPS figures given.
Alphabet: described as having its worst day ever as hyperscaler credit weakened. No earnings figures given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Driven almost entirely by energy and supports the Fed's September hike and the odds of another hike.
Core has stayed parked while headline jumped on energy.
Market pricing implies another hike despite the October pause.
Persistently high oil drives inflation and the restrictive policy path, and markets treat it as transitory pending a US-Iran deal.
Signals some relief on the funding-cost argument after the Fed pause.

trade_ideas.description: Buy CDX IG receivers to play a seasonally supported year-end rally
trade_ideas.rationale: Upside vol in credit has remained sticky and has not picked up meaningfully, and 2m receiver vol is about 36 versus a 10-year average near 41.

trade_ideas.description: Tactical compression: IG over HY, with plans to re-enter decompression at better levels
trade_ideas.rationale: Compression has been working in recent weeks, and the desk sees more room for it to run.

trade_ideas.description: Sell AI CDS (3Y AI CDS basket) versus buying NDX puts
trade_ideas.rationale: The cost of protection in credit has risen significantly in the last month versus equity for hyperscalers, so selling AI CDS against buying NDX puts is starting to look interesting.

trade_ideas.description: Hedging via payer spreads and an IG ex-hyperscaler basket
trade_ideas.rationale: Limited-loss, low-cost structures cap theta bleed.

risk_factors: Next wave of AI concern may focus on demand/ROI, so the post-Fed macro relief rally depends on the next earnings prints.
Hyperscaler capex and debt issuance are rising faster than returns, as with Amazon's negative free cash flow and $48.1B debt raise.
US-Iran negotiations could fail, with escalation raising energy prices and hurting the economy.
Oil near $100 keeps headline inflation high and the Fed hiking path alive, and an 80% December hike probability is priced.
CCC credit spreads are in the 96th percentile and AI default protection is at triple January's level.

Goldman valuation dashboard (10-year percentiles): CDX IG and HY retraced from 2026 wides (69th and 74th percentile) to the high 50s, HYG at the 10th percentile, USD CCC cash at the 96th percentile versus the 51st at 2026 wides.
Chart shows 2m CDX IG receiver vol at about 36 versus a 10-year average of almost 41.
Chart shows Goldman's compression gauge rebounding from roughly -70 in late August to a 12-month high in mid-October before giving back some of the move.
vol_and_positioning: Gross positioning in credit is light and clients are directionless. Long equity/short credit and decomp are consensus trades, and a squeeze tighter would be painful for most.
Upside vol in credit remains sticky and has not picked up meaningfully. 2m CDX IG receiver vol is about 36, below its 10-year average of almost 41.
Goldman's compression gauge rebounded from roughly -70 in late August to a 12-month high in mid-October before giving back some of the move.
NDX 1-year 10-delta put is at about 505 versus a June peak near 590, while the 3Y AI CDS basket is about 100bps, nearly triple the ~35bps at the start of the year.
For hedgers, Goldman prefers limited-loss, low-cost structures such as payer spreads and an IG ex-hyperscaler basket to cap theta bleed.
geopolitical: US-Iran negotiations: a deal has been 'close' for about seven months. This week brought a new Qatari draft that Tehran called 'unacceptable', a Vance letter to an Iranian 'hardliner', and a US warning to the Gulf to prepare for a 'short, intense' campaign after the midterms.
Iran's parliament speaker repeated the same seven conditions, and oil bounced back to $100 after dipping on diplomacy Thursday.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's rates desk warned two weeks ago that higher yields are starting to break things, with the biggest crack running through AI debt.
Goldman's Louis Miller warned two weeks ago that AI credit was pricing in a 15% drop for hyperscaler stocks.
Goldman's strategists said this week that the AI boom now lives or dies in the credit market.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is light, the Fed has paused, and the consensus is short. Goldman is cautiously optimistic that a squeeze tighter is the path of least resistance into year end, helped by receivers and falling funding-cost fears.
tension_points.bear_case: If the next wave of AI concern is about demand and ROI, the relief rally is only as good as the next earnings print, and Amazon just showed $33.5B of cash burn. CCCs are in the 96th percentile and AI default protection is at triple January's level.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A US-Iran deal collapsing into the 'short, intense' campaign, or another weak hyperscaler earnings print showing cash burn without ROI.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman sees selling AI CDS versus buying NDX puts as interesting because credit protection has become much more expensive than equity protection.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit is pricing in a roughly 15% drop for hyperscaler stocks, and the widening gap could be an early warning that equities are mispriced.
